name: Lync
label: K
lede: An Olympia trio that lasted about two years, made one album on K Records, and sent its members into Beck, Built to Spill and Modest Mouse's orbit.

eras.title: Three kids, a four-track and a stack of 7-inches
eras.text: Sam Jayne, James Bertram and Dave Schneider start Lync in Olympia, in 1992 according to Wikipedia and AllMusic. They put out singles on tiny labels while the town's K Records crowd watches from the next basement over.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lync · AllMusic: Lync biography · Suicide Squeeze: These Are Not Fall Colors reissue
years.h: [[Lync|65e1b41c-c719-4237-9f72-c2f07ea19355]] starts in Olympia: Jayne, Bertram, Schneider
years.p: Sam Jayne sings and plays guitar, James Bertram plays bass and sings, Dave Schneider plays drums.
years.xp:
Wikipedia and AllMusic date the band to 1992. Wikipedia describes the sound as distortion, cryptic lyrics and irregular tuning, with comparisons to Fugazi, Unwound and Drive Like Jehu.

Suicide Squeeze, which reissued the album, calls them a Puget Sound trio that pulled in DC, San Diego and Olympia DIY influences.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lync · Wikipedia: Remembering the Fireballs (Part 8)
years.h: Four singles on four labels: "Firestarter", "Mhz", "Pigeons", "Two Feet in Front"
years.p: "Firestarter" is a split 7-inch with Excuse 17 on Candy Ass; "Mhz" and "Pigeons" come out on Magic Pail ("Mhz" with Landspeed).
years.xp:
Per Wikipedia, "Firestarter", "Mhz" and "Pigeons" are all 1993 releases. "Two Feet in Front" follows in 1994 on K Records, the label that then puts out the album.

Tracks from these sessions, recorded by Pat Maley at yo yo capitol in early 1993 and by Tim Green at the red house in late 1993, end up on the 1997 compilation Remembering the Fireballs (Part 8).

eras.title: Beck, a basement, one album
eras.text: Jayne and Bertram play on Beck's One Foot in the Grave and then record Lync's only full-length. By the end of the year the band is done.

years.src: Wikipedia: One Foot in the Grave (Beck album) · Wikipedia: Lync
years.h: Jayne and Bertram turn up on Beck's One Foot in the Grave
years.p: K Records puts out [[Beck|309c62ba-7a22-4277-9f67-4a162526d18a]]'s album on June 27, 1994, recorded at Calvin Johnson's basement studio in Olympia.
years.xp: Wikipedia lists the album as recorded in October 1993 and January 1994 at Dub Narcotic Studio, then in [[Calvin Johnson|cac7a688-14a8-46c3-8fc8-11cca866677c]]'s basement. Its personnel list has Bertram on bass and Jayne on vocals; Wikipedia's Lync article says both performed on it. The Lync page does not say who did what on which track.

years.src: Wikipedia: These Are Not Fall Colors · Suicide Squeeze: These Are Not Fall Colors reissue
years.h: These Are Not Fall Colors is recorded in Seattle
years.p: John and Stu's Place is the room; Phil Ek, Tim Green, Calvin Johnson and the band share producing and engineering credits.
years.xp:
Wikipedia dates the sessions to spring and summer 1994. The album runs 10 tracks and 42:32, from "B" to the 6:46 closer "Uberrima Fides".

Suicide Squeeze notes that Ek, the engineer, later worked with Fleet Foxes, Band of Horses and the Shins.

years.src: Wikipedia: These Are Not Fall Colors · Suicide Squeeze: These Are Not Fall Colors reissue
years.h: These Are Not Fall Colors · K Records
years.p: Lync's only album comes out on CD, LP and cassette. Pitchfork later gave it 8.7.
years.xp: Pitchfork wrote that it "unspools like a collection of song sketches" that Jayne, Bertram and Schneider "pummeled into working shape." Trouser Press was cooler, calling it "not really good, but far from bad." The A.V. Club praised the ragged ambient loops of spoken-word samples and guitar feedback holding it together.

years.src: Wikipedia: Lync · Suicide Squeeze: These Are Not Fall Colors reissue · Wikipedia: Remembering the Fireballs (Part 8)
years.h: Lync breaks up months after the album
years.p: Wikipedia dates the split to late 1994. Suicide Squeeze puts the band's whole life at two years.
years.xp: None of the sources I found gives a reason for the split. A live recording from Gilman Street in Berkeley, mid-1994, is the last track on Remembering the Fireballs (Part 8).

eras.title: Three bands out of one
eras.text: Bertram forms Red Stars Theory and tours with Built to Spill; Schneider joins him in Built to Spill's touring band; Jayne goes solo on a four-track and calls it Love as Laughter.

years.src: Wikipedia: Red Stars Theory · Wikipedia: Lync
years.h: James Bertram starts Red Stars Theory in Seattle
years.p: [[Red Stars Theory|a9d2b2fe-b01c-4115-803c-0514ef05f8ff]] includes [[Jeremiah Green|7c84fd8e-1087-48c6-bd3d-b865819b5306]], Modest Mouse's drummer, and runs through 2000.
years.xp: Per Wikipedia, the band made two albums, But Sleep Came Slowly (1997) and Life in a Bubble Can Be Beautiful (1999), on labels including Deluxe, Rx Remedy, Touch and Go and Suicide Squeeze. Green and Bertram both had other bands (Modest Mouse and 764-HERO), which limited how much Red Stars Theory could tour. Wikipedia's Lync article adds that Bertram later co-founded the label and merch company Luckyhorse Industries.

years.src: Wikipedia: The Normal Years · Wikipedia: Lync
years.h: [[Built to Spill|3ac482b8-1494-4071-a0e9-f192f9d2c2b0]]'s The Normal Years features Bertram and Schneider
years.p: K Records' odds-and-ends collection includes "Some", recorded live at Chicago Filmmaker in mid-1995, with both ex-Lync players.
years.xp: Wikipedia credits Schneider with drums on the track. Both Bertram and Schneider toured with Built to Spill in the mid-1990s, according to Wikipedia's Lync article.

years.src: Stereogum: Love As Laughter's Sam Jayne Dead At 46 · AllMusic: Lync biography · Wikipedia: Love as Laughter · Variety: Sam Jayne, Frontman of Love as Laughter, Dies at 46 · Spin: Sam Jayne and the Plight of Indie Musicians
years.h: Sam Jayne starts Love as Laughter as a four-track project
years.p: Stereogum and AllMusic date it to 1996; it grows into a full band by 1998.
years.xp:
Wikipedia's Love as Laughter article says the project began in 1994, right after Lync; Stereogum and AllMusic say 1996. By 1998, per Stereogum, it was a full band based in New York, and it went on to record for K, Sub Pop and [[Isaac Brock|071d3d16-8ed7-4e06-be96-2c52defcf434]]'s Glacial Pace. Wikipedia says Schneider contributed to the early releases.

Variety reports that Jayne was also briefly a member of [[Modest Mouse|a96ac800-bfcb-412a-8a63-0a98df600700]]; Spin says he played maracas with them on Saturday Night Live in 2004.

years.src: Wikipedia: Remembering the Fireballs (Part 8) · Wikipedia: Lync
years.p: K and Troubleman Unlimited gather the singles and unreleased songs, recorded across 1993 and 1994.
years.xp: Wikipedia's credits split the sources: tracks 1 to 5 recorded by Pat Maley in early 1993, tracks 6 to 12 by Tim Green in late 1993, track 13 at John and Stu's Place in mid-1994, and track 14 live at Gilman in mid-1994. Bertram and Maley are the producers.

eras.title: The record gets its second life
eras.text: Jayne dies in December 2020. Three years later Suicide Squeeze reissues the album.

years.src: Variety: Sam Jayne, Frontman of Love as Laughter, Dies at 46 · Stereogum: Love As Laughter's Sam Jayne Dead At 46 · Spin: Sam Jayne and the Plight of Indie Musicians · Brooklyn Vegan: Sam Jayne of Love as Laughter has died · Wikipedia: Love as Laughter
years.h: Sam Jayne is found dead in New York at 46
years.p: Variety reported he was found in his car; Spin reported his family said the cause was heart-related, undiagnosed conditions.
years.xp:
Stereogum and Spin report he was reported missing on December 6 and found on December 15; Brooklyn Vegan and Variety give December 7 as the last contact. Bandmate Zeke Howard confirmed the news on Instagram. Stereogum reported no signs of foul play.

Spin reported that Jayne had been bartending in Brooklyn, including at Clem's in Williamsburg, where he ran a weekly music-video night, and that during the pandemic he was living between a few places, according to Howard. Fleet Foxes' Robin Pecknold called him "an elusive and formatively inspiring hero," as quoted by Brooklyn Vegan.

years.src: Suicide Squeeze: These Are Not Fall Colors reissue · Wikipedia: These Are Not Fall Colors
years.h: Suicide Squeeze reissues These Are Not Fall Colors as a double LP
years.p: Remastered, with a bonus track ("Can't Tie Yet"), a gatefold, an 18x24 poster and liner notes by Brian Cook.
years.xp: Three vinyl variants: 250 half-and-half copies for the band, 250 twist copies for the label, 1,000 color-in-color for retail. Jesse LeDoux expanded the artwork; Phil Ek's original recording was remastered.
